cohort- and baseline-referenced manner.

the SGP package (v2.2.2.0).
• All analyses ran without error or warning.

Goodness of Fit Plots
• SGP Goodness of Fit plots indicate the distribution of state calculated SGPs by grade and
content area (for example, grade 5, mathematics).
• By definition, cohort referenced SGPs should for a uniform distribution with the same
number of students receiving SGPs of 1, 2, 3, …, 99. Any deviation from a uniform
distribution indicates model misfit.
• Baseline referenced SGPs need not have a uniform distribution since we are using
previously calculated growth norms with current data.
• We want to see higher percentages of students demonstrating higher rates of
growth.
• We want to see lower percentages of students demonstrating lower rates of growth.
• However, deviations from uniformity in baseline SGPs can also signal scale drift/shift.

Goodness of Fit Plots
• SGP Goodness of Fit plots indicate the distribution of state calculated SGPs by grade and
content area (for example, grade 5, mathematics).
• By definition, cohort referenced SGPs should for a uniform distribution with the same
number of students receiving SGPs of 1, 2, 3, …, 99. Any deviation from a uniform
distribution indicates model misfit.
• Baseline referenced SGPs need not have a uniform distribution since we are using
previously calculated growth norms with current data.
• We want to see higher percentages of students demonstrating higher rates of
growth.
• We want to see lower percentages of students demonstrating lower rates of growth.
• However, deviations from uniformity in baseline SGPs can also signal scale drift/shift.
